description: The bar chart compares the accuracy (%) of a model across different configurations on two datasets, PHEME and PolitiFact, with each dataset shown in a separate panel. The vertical axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 75.0 to 95.0, with major gridlines at 2.5% intervals. The horizontal axis lists various experimental conditions, including "Ours," "w/o text," "w/o select," "w/o emotion," and "w/o cognition," with "Ours" representing the full model and the others indicating ablation studies where a specific component is removed. In the PHEME panel, the "Ours" model achieves the highest accuracy at 89.84%, followed by "w/o select" at 88.80%, "w/o emotion" at 87.34%, "w/o cognition" at 87.17%, and "w/o text" at 86.82%. In the PolitiFact panel, the "Ours" model again shows the highest accuracy at 90.57%, followed by "w/o select" at 89.62%, "w/o cognition" at 87.74%, "w/o emotion" at 84.91%, "w/o text" at 83.02%, and "w/o comments" at 85.85%. The bars are color-coded: dark red for "Ours," light red for "w/o comments," orange for "w/o text," light blue for "w/o select," medium blue for "w/o emotion," and dark blue for "w/o cognition." The chart clearly demonstrates that removing any component leads to a decrease in accuracy, with the "w/o text" and "w/o select" conditions showing the most significant drops.
